class.name: VGMStream
class.brief_description: Plays sound chip music logs (VGM/VGZ, S98, DRO, GYM, SPC, NSF/NSFe) by emulating the original sound chips with libvgm.
class.description: Files with the extensions [code].vgm[/code], [code].vgz[/code], [code].s98[/code], [code].dro[/code], [code].gym[/code], [code].spc[/code], [code].nsf[/code] and [code].nsfe[/code] load as [VGMStream] resources: assign one to an [AudioStreamPlayer] (or 2D/3D variant), or [method @GDScript.load] it from a script. Songs that use a chip with no permissively licensed core (the Virtual Boy VSU, MSM5232 or ES5506) fail to load. All settings live on the stream and apply live to every playback of it: [member speed], [member loop_count], [member fade_time], [member ignore_song_volume], [member resampler_mode], and for each sound chip (a "device") its emulation option bits, channel muting and channel panning. To give players of the same song different values without [method Resource.duplicate], use the stream parameters below. In the inspector, each chip of the song has its own group with a checkbox per channel to mute it, its named emulation options (filters and other flags) and, when the chip's emulation supports it, a pan slider per channel. These are dynamic properties named [code]chip_<index>_muted_channels[/code], [code]chip_<index>_options[/code] and [code]chip_<index>_pan_<channel>[/code]; the methods below do the same from scripts. [codeblock] var song: VGMStream = load("res://music/stage1.vgz") $AudioStreamPlayer.stream = song $AudioStreamPlayer.play() song.speed = 1.25 # Faster tempo, same pitch. song.set_channel_muted(0, 2, true) # Mute channel 3 of the first chip. [/codeblock] [b]Per-player parameters:[/b] every [AudioStreamPlayer] showing a [VGMStream] has a [b]Parameters[/b] section (Godot 4.3 and later), kept by that player alone: - [code]parameters/speed[/code]: multiplies [member speed]. Default [code]1.0[/code]. - [code]parameters/chip_<index>_muted_channels[/code]: channels of that chip to mute, as a bit mask. They are muted in addition to the channels muted on the stream: a player can mute more, but cannot unmute what the stream mutes. [codeblock] $PlayerA.set("parameters/speed", 2.0) $PlayerB.set("parameters/chip_0_muted_channels", 0b100) # Mute channel 3 of the first chip, on this player only. [/codeblock] [b]NSF and NSFe:[/b] the music files of the NES and Famicom. One file holds a number of songs, called tracks: choose one with [member track]. A track plays the way the console would play it, expansion chips included (VRC6, VRC7, FDS, MMC5, Namco 163, Sunsoft 5B); only an NSF can use the expansion chips other than the FDS and the VRC7, which VGM files can also drive. The length and fade of a track come from the file when it has them (NSFe); otherwise the track plays until it is stopped. [member speed] changes the tempo by calling the game's sound driver more or less often; the pitch stays, and what the chips play by themselves (the DPCM samples) keeps its speed, as with every chip. [b]Song info:[/b] [member format], [member format_version], [member loop_start], [member loop_length] and [method get_device_clock] describe the file. Loop and fade events are signals of [VGMStreamPlayback]. [member loop_count], [member fade_time], [member ignore_song_volume] and [member resampler_mode] follow the project-wide defaults in [b]Project Settings > Libvgm Settings[/b] ([code]libvgm_settings/*[/code]) until they are set on the stream. Setting one to the project's value, or reverting it in the inspector, makes it follow the project setting again. Pitch is changed with [member AudioStreamPlayer.pitch_scale]. General filtering (low-pass, high-pass, EQ) is done with audio bus effects such as [AudioEffectLowPassFilter]; [VGMStream] exposes the filtering that is part of the chip emulation (see [method set_device_core_options] and the [code]CORE_OPTION_*[/code] constants). [b]Note:[/b] Settings changed in the inspector on a stream loaded directly from a [code].vgm[/code] file are not saved back into that file. Set them from a script, or save the stream as a [code].tres[/code] resource, which stores the song data and the settings.

method.name: get_channel_names
method.description: Returns the channel names of [param device]. The array index is the channel index used by [method set_channel_muted].

method.name: get_channel_pan
method.description: Returns the stereo position of [param channel] of [param device], from [code]-1.0[/code] (left) to [code]1.0[/code] (right).

method.name: get_device_clock
method.description: Returns the clock of the sound chip [param device], in Hz, as stored in the file. A device that is part of another chip reports that chip's clock.

method.name: get_device_core_options
method.description: Returns the emulation option bits of [param device]. They start at libvgm's defaults for the song.

method.name: get_device_count
method.description: Returns the number of sound chips the song uses. Chips that are part of another chip (such as the SSG of a YM2608) are listed as their own device.

method.name: get_device_name
method.description: Returns the chip name of [param device], for example [code]"SN76496"[/code]. A second chip of the same type is suffixed with [code]" #2"[/code].

method.name: get_format
method.description: Returns the file format of the song: [code]"VGM"[/code], [code]"S98"[/code], [code]"DRO"[/code], [code]"GYM"[/code], [code]"SPC"[/code] or [code]"NSF"[/code] (for NSF and NSFe files). Empty when the stream has no data.

method.name: get_format_version
method.description: Returns the version of the file format, for example [code]"1.71"[/code]. Empty when the stream has no data.

method.name: get_loop_length
method.description: Returns the length of the looped part of the song in seconds, or [code]0[/code] if the song does not loop. See [method get_loop_start].

method.name: get_loop_start
method.description: Returns the position in seconds where the song starts to loop, or [code]0[/code] if the song does not loop. This is a position in the file, the same time base as [method AudioStreamPlayer.get_playback_position] and [method AudioStreamPlayer.seek], independent of [member speed]. To jump to the loop: [code]$AudioStreamPlayer.seek(song.get_loop_start())[/code].

method.name: get_song_tags
method.description: Returns the song's tags, such as [code]"TITLE"[/code], [code]"GAME"[/code], [code]"ARTIST"[/code] and [code]"DATE"[/code]. Only tags present in the file are included.

method.name: get_track_count
method.description: Returns the number of tracks (songs) in the file: more than one only for an NSF or NSFe file. [code]0[/code] when the stream has no data. See [member track].

method.name: has_channel_panning
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the emulation of [param device] supports per-channel panning. Panning set for other chips has no effect.

method.name: is_channel_muted
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param channel] of [param device] is muted.

method.name: set_channel_muted
method.description: Mutes or unmutes one channel of [param device]. Takes effect immediately on playing streams.

method.name: set_channel_pan
method.description: Sets the stereo position of [param channel] of [param device], from [code]-1.0[/code] (left) to [code]1.0[/code] (right). Takes effect immediately. Only applies while [method has_channel_panning] is [code]true[/code].

method.name: set_device_core_options
method.description: Sets the emulation option bits of [param device]: a combination of the [code]CORE_OPTION_*[/code] constants for that chip, or other chip-specific flags documented in libvgm's [code]emu/cores/*.h[/code] headers. The inspector shows the known flags of each chip as named checkboxes. Takes effect immediately. Devices that are part of another chip share that chip's options and cannot be set. [codeblock] # Turn off the Game Boy high-pass filter. var opts := song.get_device_core_options(0) song.set_device_core_options(0, opts & ~VGMStream.CORE_OPTION_NES_NONLINEAR_MIXER) [/codeblock]

method.name: set_device_muted
method.description: Mutes or unmutes all channels of [param device].

members.member: The raw song file (optionally gzip-compressed, as in [code].vgz[/code]). Setting it re-reads the song's devices and resets the per-device settings. Invalid data is rejected with an error and leaves the stream empty.
Storage of the per-device settings (emulation options, muted channels and panning), so they are saved with the resource. Use the device methods instead of editing it.
Length of the fade-out in seconds once [member loop_count] loops have played. [code]0.0[/code] stops immediately at the end of the last loop.
The file format of the song, shown in the inspector's [b]Song Info[/b] group. Read-only. See [method get_format].
The version of the file format. Read-only. See [method get_format_version].
If [code]true[/code], ignores the volume adjustment stored in the song file, so songs play at the chips' plain output level.

How many times songs with a loop point play through their loop before ending (followed by [member fade_time]); [code]0[/code] loops forever. VGM files can scale this count for very short or long loops. When the song ends, [signal AudioStreamPlayer.finished] is emitted.
Length of the looped part of the song, in seconds. [code]0[/code] without a loop. Read-only. See [method get_loop_length].
Position where the song starts to loop, in seconds. [code]0[/code] without a loop. Read-only. See [method get_loop_start].

Storage of the settings this stream overrides instead of following Project Settings ([member loop_count], [member fade_time], [member ignore_song_volume], [member resampler_mode]), so they are saved with the resource. Use those properties instead of editing it.
Quality of the resampling from each chip's native rate to the output rate. Playing streams restart the chip emulation and continue from their current position.

Playback tempo multiplier. Unlike [member AudioStreamPlayer.pitch_scale], this keeps the pitch unchanged. Must be greater than [code]0[/code]. For SPC files it speeds up the timers that the music driver counts its tempo with, for NSF files the calls of the driver; what the chips play by themselves (samples, DSP envelopes) keeps its speed, as with every chip.

The track (song) to play, from [code]0[/code] to [method get_track_count] [code]- 1[/code]. Only an NSF or NSFe file has more than one; the default is the one the file starts with. Setting it updates [method AudioStream.get_length], the tags of [method get_song_tags] and the loop information, and restarts every player that is playing the stream from the start of the new track. Shown in the inspector only for a file with several tracks.

constants.constant: Low quality when downsampling, high quality when upsampling.
NES APU: uses the console's nonlinear channel mixing. On by default.
Irem GA20: linear interpolation of samples.
